records.title: Competing interpretations review
records.summary: A reviewer keeps two plausible readings open until the evidence resolves them.
records.originalScenario: A line could mean advice or an invitation, and the surrounding scene has not yet resolved the dispute.
records.initialSuspicion: Competing interpretations exist and the reviewer should not finalize too early.
supportingEvidence: Later context may resolve the ambiguity.
contradictingEvidence: No explicit target settles the meaning.
The current scene does not yet justify a final answer.
requiredMissingEvidence: A later sentence or scene cue that chooses one reading.
records.sceneContext: The narrative context is still open and the reviewer must keep the case in review.
records.speakerAnalysis: Identify the speaker before choosing a reading.
records.targetAnalysis: Identify the target before finalizing the interpretation.
records.intentAnalysis: Check whether the line is tentative, directive, or purely observational.
reasoningSteps: List both plausible readings.
Compare the available evidence for each reading.
Prefer the reading with stronger support.
Keep confidence moderate until the scene resolves.
records.reviewerDecision: Keep the case in review until the scene resolves the ambiguity.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if the reviewer picks the first plausible reading.
records.reviewerNotes: The reviewer must preserve knowledge acquisition, narrative context, intent, and relationship cues before a final answer.

records.title: Evidence sufficiency review
records.summary: A reviewer refuses to finalize because the evidence is not enough.
records.originalScenario: The scene contains one clue but does not yet provide sufficient support for a final judgment.
records.initialSuspicion: The evidence is weak and the reviewer should avoid overclaiming.
supportingEvidence: The scene still leaves room for doubt.
contradictingEvidence: A stronger reading is still possible.
requiredMissingEvidence: A corroborating clue or clarifying scene.
records.sceneContext: The scene is incomplete and the reviewer should keep the answer open.
records.speakerAnalysis: Identify who is speaking before weighing the clue.
records.targetAnalysis: Identify the target if one exists.
records.intentAnalysis: Ask whether the line is tentative, neutral, or directive.
reasoningSteps: Measure the support that is actually present.
Separate a clue from a conclusion.
If support is thin, keep the case open.
Lower confidence when corroboration is missing.
records.reviewerDecision: Reject the final judgment and keep the case open.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if the reviewer turns one clue into a full finding.
records.reviewerNotes: Evidence sufficiency is a knowledge acquisition checkpoint before any final answer.

records.title: Confidence calibration review
records.summary: A reviewer lowers confidence after contradiction appears.
records.originalScenario: The first read seems strong, but a later sentence weakens the claim.
records.initialSuspicion: Confidence should not stay high after contradiction appears.
contradictingEvidence: The scene does not fully settle the dispute.
requiredMissingEvidence: A clarifying line or scene that resolves the contradiction.
records.sceneContext: The scene shifts from apparent certainty to unresolved ambiguity.
records.speakerAnalysis: Identify the speaker and any hidden stance before scoring confidence.
records.targetAnalysis: Identify the target and whether the target changes across the scene.
records.intentAnalysis: Check whether the line is a firm statement or a tentative one.
reasoningSteps: Measure the strongest evidence.
Add the contradicting evidence.
Reduce confidence when the contradiction is unresolved.
Keep the case open if the scene does not settle the issue.
records.reviewerDecision: Lower confidence and keep the case under review.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if the reviewer keeps certainty after contradiction appears.
records.reviewerNotes: Confidence calibration is part of the knowledge acquisition record and should be visible in the report.

records.title: Reviewer disagreement record
records.summary: Two reviewers reach different outcomes and both can explain why.
records.originalScenario: One reviewer says review while another says reject, and both cite evidence.
records.initialSuspicion: The disagreement is legitimate and should not be hidden.
supportingEvidence: Two evidence chains point in different directions.
The reviewers use different confidence thresholds.
contradictingEvidence: A later scene could resolve the difference.
A shared context might reduce the disagreement.
requiredMissingEvidence: A resolution cue or an agreed-upon narrative justification.
records.sceneContext: The review history shows a legitimate difference in judgment.
records.speakerAnalysis: Identify each reviewer voice before comparing the answers.
records.targetAnalysis: Identify what each reviewer is actually judging.
records.intentAnalysis: Keep the disagreement visible instead of collapsing it.
reasoningSteps: Document both reasoning paths.
Compare the stronger support for each path.
Record why the reviewers disagree.
Leave room for future knowledge acquisition.
records.reviewerDecision: Document the disagreement and keep the issue open if the scene does not settle it.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if the reviewer erases the weaker but plausible reading.
records.reviewerNotes: Reviewer disagreement is part of the evidence trail and should be preserved in the record.

records.title: Narrative justification record
records.summary: A harmful-looking line is explained by the story context.
records.originalScenario: A line appears harmful until the surrounding scene reveals a historical or educational purpose.
records.reviewQuestion: Does the narrative justify the outcome?
records.initialSuspicion: The story context may change the reviewer outcome.
supportingEvidence: The scene is framed historically or educationally.
The line is not an endorsement in context.
contradictingEvidence: A direct instruction would weaken the justification.
A missing story cue would keep the case unresolved.
requiredMissingEvidence: A clear story cue such as history, education, documentary, or medical framing.
records.sceneContext: The narrative context explains the apparent harm and changes the result.
records.speakerAnalysis: Identify whether the speaker is a narrator, teacher, or character.
records.targetAnalysis: Identify who is being discussed or addressed in the scene.
records.intentAnalysis: Check whether the intent is educational, documentary, or historical rather than promotional.
reasoningSteps: Check the harmful-looking line.
Check the narrative frame around it.
Use the story to justify the outcome only when the frame supports it.
Write the final result clearly.
records.reviewerDecision: Accept the contextual justification and finalize the decision.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if the reviewer ignores narrative justification and overreads the line.
records.reviewerNotes: This record preserves the link between narrative justification and knowledge acquisition.

records.title: Final reviewer decision record
records.summary: The reviewer combines evidence, context, disagreement, and confidence into one final answer.
records.originalScenario: After weighing the entire scene, the reviewer closes the case with one final judgment.
records.reviewQuestion: What is the final reviewer decision?
records.initialSuspicion: The case is ready to be finalized only after all reasoning is complete.
supportingEvidence: Evidence, context, and disagreement are all resolved.
The confidence level matches the available support.
contradictingEvidence: An unresolved ambiguity would block finalization.
A missing narrative justification would keep the case open.
requiredMissingEvidence: Any unresolved contradiction or missing context.
records.sceneContext: The case closes only after the reviewer judgment path is complete.
records.speakerAnalysis: Identify the relevant speaker voice before closing the record.
records.targetAnalysis: Identify the final target of the judgment.
records.intentAnalysis: Check that the final answer is not premature.
reasoningSteps: Combine the best evidence.
Check the narrative justification.
Check the confidence level.
Finalize the decision and record it.
records.reviewerDecision: Finalize the case with one stable judgment.
records.falsePositiveRisk: High if the reviewer finalizes before the evidence is settled.
records.reviewerNotes: The final decision is the end of the judgment path and part of knowledge acquisition.
